h1: Riveting machines — hydraulic orbital riveters, rivets to Ø1-3/16″
intro: An orbital (rolling) riveting machine forms the head of a solid rivet by rolling the rivet end into shape instead of hammering it, with about a tenth of the force of punch riveting: the part keeps its fit and the head comes out smooth, without vibration or noise. It replaces hammering, punching and hot riveting on hinges, chain links, brake parts, appliances and hardware, and with other tools the machine works as a normal press. NovoTech's value-line XM riveters, built in China, come in six sizes, small to large, for solid rivets from Ø3/16″ (XM-5, 1,911 lbf) to Ø1-3/16″ (XM-30, 22,481 lbf), with 11 rivet head forms and tables from Ø4.7″ to 19.7 × 14″. The specification table and photo are below. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Which XM riveter for my rivet?
faq.a: Choose by the largest solid rivet you set: XM-5 to Ø3/16″, XM-8 to Ø5/16″, XM-10 to Ø3/8″, XM-16 to Ø5/8″, XM-20 to Ø13/16″ and XM-30 to Ø1-3/16″. Send us a drawing of the part and the rivet and we confirm the size and the head form.

faq.q: Orbital riveting or pressing the rivet?
faq.a: Pressing or punching sets the whole head at once and needs about ten times the force, which can distort the part and loosen the fit. The orbital head rolls the rivet end outward a little at a time, so the force stays low, the head comes out smooth and the part keeps its fit — the reason it is used for hinges, chain links and brake parts.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
